inputs.coverage: Convex light-curve reconstruction with approximate thermal size: 143.77 km effective diameter (catalog ±2.51 km; additional shape and thermal-model uncertainty). Thermal size is used as a volume-scale approximation. An alternative pole remains possible. The grid marks unavailable imagery; rotational phase is illustrative. The physical size is approximately calibrated by assigning the AKARI thermal effective diameter to the mesh volume-equivalent diameter. Neither source mesh nor spin is modified. Convex inversion supplies only broad outline; no resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture can be inferred. Hanuš2021 TableA.2 reports316 ASAS-SN observations and both poles(173,-7)/(355,13). Its catalog diameter128.7 km differs from AKARI143.77 km; neither number is established as this mesh physical volume. The pinned AKARI effective diameter is used only as a stated scale approximation.
